InnoPharm Biotech - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the InnoPharm Biotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during listen-only mode. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss InnoPharm Biotech's financial results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Michael Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Lisa Rodriguez, Head of Commercial; Tom Berger, Head of Manufacturing; and Karen Lee, Head of Regulatory Affairs.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale, CEO of InnoPharm Biotech.

Johnathan Hale, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. InnoPharm Biotech delivered a strong performance in the Q3, driven by robust demand for our oncology and rare disease franchises, including standout growth from InnoTarget and GeneForge. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities.

Today, I will provide an overview of our performance and strategic initiatives, focusing on the pricing and reimbursement landscape, product revenue by key drug franchise with volume and price analysis, cash flow and balance sheet highlights, strategic priorities and outlook, regulatory approvals and label expansions achieved, gross margin trends and manufacturing efficiency, operating expense analysis, and patent cliff exposure and life cycle management strategies.

We are particularly excited about NovaLume and its potential to transform frontline NSCLC treatment with blockbuster potential.

Now, I will turn the call over to John Ramirez, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

John Ramirez, CFO:
Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid Q3. Revenue for the quarter was $2.8 billion, an increase of 18% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by volume growth in oncology and rare diseases, favorable product mix, and geographic expansion, partially offset by pricing pressures.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $1.20 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $550 million, or $1.50 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.8 billion, reflecting continued investment in our pipeline while achieving leverage through efficiencies. We continue to invest in R&D to support our pipeline. Our cash position remains strong at $2.8 billion.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to total revenue of $11.0-11.5 billion, non-GAAP EPS of $5.80-6.20, reflecting oncology momentum and manufacturing gains.

Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning, everyone. Turning now to the pricing and reimbursement landscape, which continues to be a dynamic and critical driver of our financial performance here at InnoPharm Biotech. As you know, we specialize in next-generation targeted therapies for oncology and rare genetic disorders, with our portfolio anchored by our blockbuster PD-L1 inhibitor, InnoTarget, generating over $2.8 billion in global net sales last year, alongside our recently launched gene therapy, GeneForge, for spinal muscular atrophy, or SMA, which is ramping to projected peak sales of $1.2 billion.

Let me start with the U.S., which accounts for 68% of our revenue and remains the most scrutinized market. We've seen persistent pricing pressures from the Inflation Reduction Act, or IRA, particularly the Medicare Drug Price Negotiation program starting in 2026. For InnoTarget, our Wholesale Acquisition Cost, or WAC, stands at $185,000 per year of therapy, but our realized net price per patient was $142,000 in Q3—down 4.2% year-over-year—reflecting higher gross-to-net adjustments of 23%, driven by increased rebates to PBMs like Express Scripts and CVS Caremark, now averaging 18% off list for commercial channels. In Medicare Part D, where InnoTarget has strong uptake among NSCLC patients, we're modeling a 12-15% price concession under the first negotiation tranche, similar to what Eli Lilly faced with Mounjaro analogs.

Positively, our 340B discount liability grew to $450 million in Q3, up 15% sequentially, as safety-net hospitals expand access—we've mitigated erosion through enhanced contract pharmacy oversight via our Value360 program, limiting passthrough leakage to under 5%. On reimbursement, CMS's 2024 ASP updates held steady at 96% of WAC for InnoTarget, supporting Q4 durability, while GeneForge secured J-code assignment in September, accelerating hospital buy-in with a net price realization of $1.95 million per dose versus $2.3 million WAC. We've also inked outcomes-based rebate agreements with three of the top five PBMs, tying 8% of InnoTarget rebates to ORR and PFS endpoints from our real-world evidence, or RWE, datasets—early data shows 92% threshold attainment, shielding us from the 10-15% ASP declines seen in peers like Bristol Myers' Opdivo post-patent cliffs.

Shifting to ex-U.S., which drove 32% of sales and grew 11% YoY in constant currency, the landscape is bifurcated. In Europe, comprising 18% of revenue, HTA bodies remain rigorous: NICE in the UK granted full reimbursement for InnoTarget in H1NCDA last quarter at a 7% discount to list, while Germany's IQWiG approved GeneForge with an early benefit assessment score of 3 (considerable added benefit), enabling AMNOG pricing at €1.8 million per dose. However, France's HAS imposed a 22% clawback on InnoTarget due to comparator data versus Merck's Keytruda, pressuring ASPs to €145,000. We've countered with our EU RWE Hub, submitting 18-month post-launch data from 4,500 patients, which lifted reimbursement in Italy's AIFA from partial to full, adding €120 million in annualized value.

In Japan, PMDA reimbursement for InnoTarget holds at JPY 28 million per course, with NHI price revisions capped at -2.1% for FY2024—better than the -5.5% cuts to Roche's Tecentriq. China, a high-growth frontier at 6% of ex-US sales, saw InnoTarget added to the NRDL in September at a 52% discount to U.S. WAC, aligning with the aggressive volume-for-price model that boosted Novo Nordisk's Ozempic uptake 300% post-inclusion. GeneForge is in NRDL negotiations, targeting Q1 2025 entry with modeled net pricing of RMB 12 million per dose.

Emerging markets like Brazil and India contribute 4% but face headwinds: ANVISA reimbursement for InnoTarget lags at 65% coverage, prompting our patient access programs, which covered 1,200 patients YTD via co-pay caps at $5,000 annually.

Strategically, we're ahead of the curve with three key initiatives. First, our Biosimilar Defense Strategy: With Humira-like erosion patterns looming for InnoTarget in 2027, we've filed three composition-of-matter patents and launched a patent thicket of 22, while partnering with payers on step-edit protocols that delay biosimilar uptake by 6-9 months, as seen with Janssen's Stelara. Second, Value-Based Contracting 2.0: 25% of our U.S. book-of-business now under risk-sharing deals, leveraging our proprietary OutcomesLink platform for claims-level PFS adjudication—Q3 performance yielded $65 million in rebate reversals. Third, Global Pricing Corridors: We've harmonized ex-US ASPs to 45-55% of U.S. net, optimizing launch sequencing with U.S. first for cash flow, then EU tenders, and finally NRDL volume ramps.

Looking forward, we expect gross-to-net to stabilize at 22-24% in 2025, with U.S. net price growth of +1-2% excluding IRA, offset by +8% volume from label expansions. Risks include potential IRA expansion to Part B drugs like GeneForge and EU joint clinical assessments post-2025, but our $1.1 billion R&D pipeline—including three bispecifics in Phase 3—positions us for premium pricing via superior efficacy.

Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning, everyone. I'll now turn to our Q3 product revenue performance, with a deep dive into our key franchises. As you know, we categorize our portfolio into four primary franchises: Oncology, Immunology, Rare Diseases, and Emerging Therapies. Total product net sales for the quarter came in at $2.65 billion, up 18% year-over-year on a reported basis and 20% at constant currency. This strong topline was driven by a healthy mix of volume expansion, modest pricing tailwinds, and favorable geographic mix, partially offset by the anticipated biosimilar erosion in our legacy Immunology assets.

Excluding the one-time $150 million milestone from our GT-234 gene therapy partnership with Roche—recognized in Rare Diseases—our core operational growth was 14%. U.S. net sales represented 82% of the total, or $2.17 billion, up 19% YoY, fueled by robust demand and share gains in high-value segments. Ex-U.S. grew 15% to $480 million, with Europe at +22% on accelerated launches and Japan up 12% despite reimbursement headwinds.

Let me break this down franchise-by-franchise, including volume, price, and mix dynamics. We'll reference IQVIA National Sales Perspectives for U.S. TRx and NRx data, and our internal global IQVIA MAT analytics.

Oncology Franchise: $1.28 billion, +28% YoY (48% of total revenue)  
Oncology continues to be our growth engine, delivering $1.28 billion in Q3 net sales, up 28% reported and 30% ex-FX. This franchise benefits from our next-gen PD-1/PD-L1 portfolio, led by ONC-451, our bispecific antibody now approved in five indications including frontline NSCLC and adjuvant melanoma—mirroring the label expansions we've seen with peers like Merck's Keytruda or BMS's Opdivo.

- Volume: +22% YoY, with U.S. TRx up 18% to 145,000 scripts and NRx share expanding 320 basis points to 24% in metastatic NSCLC per IQVIA NBRx. Ex-U.S., volumes surged 35% on EMA and PMDA approvals for the bispecific combo with our CTLA-4 inhibitor, ONC-267. Patient days on therapy increased 25%, driven by improved durability data from our Phase 3 VISTA-3 trial readout earlier this year.
  
- Pricing: +5% ASP growth to $14,200 per patient-month in the U.S., supported by 4% list price increases and a favorable payer mix shift toward commercial lives (now 62% vs. 55% LY). We realized $20 million in Q3 from our patient assistance programs optimizing rebates. Ex-U.S., ASP was flat at €11,500 due to German AMNOG rebating, but Japan saw +8% on JPY pricing stability.

Strategic tailwinds include our manufacturing scale-up at the new Singapore facility, which reduced COGS by 15% via continuous perfusion bioreactors, enabling us to capture 2 points of share from Roche's Tecentriq in EU frontline settings. Looking ahead, ONC-451's sBLA for hepatocellular carcinoma, with data expected Q4, could add $500 million in peak U.S. sales by 2026.

Immunology Franchise: $780 million, +6% YoY (29% of total revenue)  
Immunology net sales reached $780 million, up 6% YoY, but core growth excluding biosimilar impact was +12%. Our anchor, IMM-789 (anti-IL-23 for psoriasis and IBD), faced $120 million in U.S. biosimilar erosion from Amgen's ENIA and Samsung Bioepis's launches—similar to the Humira cliff we all navigated last year.

- Volume: Flat overall at +1%, with U.S. TRx down 8% to 220,000 amid the switch, but NRx share stabilized at 16% in moderate-to-severe psoriasis. Ex-U.S., volumes grew 15%, led by +25% in China post-NMPA approval and IMM-789's first IBD label there. Global patient starts on therapy rose 4% sequentially, bolstered by our SC-to-IV switch data reducing injection burden.

- Pricing: +5% U.S. ASP to $2,800 per 4-week dose, via 3.5% WAC hikes and gross-to-net improvements from 48% to 46%—aided by our Value-Based Agreement with CVS Caremark tying rebates to 12-month persistence rates. Europe ASP dipped 2% to €2,100 on clawback provisions, but we offset with 300 bps mix shift to higher-margin IBD.

Initiatives like our digital adherence platform, integrated with Apple HealthKit, drove a 10% uplift in refill rates, positioning us to defend share against AbbVie's Skyrizi in the $15 billion IL-23 market. We're guiding 5-8% growth for FY24 as biosimilar penetration plateaus at 35%.

Rare Diseases Franchise: $420 million, +42% YoY (16% of total revenue)  
Rare Diseases exploded to $420 million, up 42% YoY, including the Roche milestone. Ex-milestone, +28%, led by GTX-234, our AAV gene therapy for hemophilia A—now with 18 months of durable FIX expression data akin to BioMarin's Roctavian.

- Volume: +32% YoY, with 1,200 global treatments to date; U.S. uptake accelerated post-Type IIIB label, capturing 22% share vs. standard factor VIII per Spherix analytics. Ex-U.S., +45% with first EU patients dosed under early access and Japan launch Q1.

- Pricing: U.S. ASP steady at $3.2 million per treatment (one-time curative), with gross-to-net at 32% reflecting specialty pharmacy efficiencies. Ex-U.S., €2.8 million with volume-based discounts in Horizon 2020 negotiations.

Our lentiviral vector process improvements cut production costs 20%, enabling $100 million in FY24 guidance upside. Partnerships like Roche's co-promotion in hemophilia B expand our reach into a $12 billion TAM.

Emerging Therapies Franchise: $170 million, +15% YoY (6% of total revenue; Other: 1%)  
Emerging Therapies, including our early Alzheimer's candidate ALZ-112 and RSV mAb RSV-345, grew 15% to $170 million. Volumes up 12% on pediatric RSV uptake (U.S. TRx +20% vs. GSK's Beyfortus), with ASP +2% amid Medicaid rebate stability.

In aggregate, volumes drove 12 points of growth, pricing/mix 8 points, with FX a 2-point tailwind. Biosimilar pressures were contained to 4% of total revenue, while label expansions and manufacturing efficiencies added 300 bps to margins. We're raising FY24 product revenue guidance to $10.6-10.9 billion, implying 17-20% growth, with Oncology pacing at 25%+.

Regionally, U.S. Medicare Part D redesign poses a 2-3% ASP risk in 2025, but our 85% commercial exposure mitigates this versus peers. Ex-U.S., we're targeting 25% CAGR through 2027 via China/Japan ramps and EMA Type II variations.

Thank you, Johnathan. Good afternoon, everyone. I'll now walk you through our Q3 cash flow and balance sheet highlights, which underscore the strengthening financial foundation of InnoPharm Biotech as we execute on our high-margin oncology and rare disease franchise. Our balance sheet remains rock-solid, providing ample firepower for our late-stage pipeline, including the upcoming PDUFA for OncoTarget-7 in Q1 next year, while our operating cash flows reflect the durable revenue ramp from ZenoVax, our approved CAR-T therapy for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, now generating over $800 million in quarterly run-rate sales.

Starting with the balance sheet as of September 30th. We ended the quarter with $2.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities, up 18% sequentially from $2.4 billion at Q2 end. This positions us with a pro-forma cash runway well exceeding 4 years at current burn rates, even before anticipated milestones from our partnerships with Regeneron and Takeda. Excluding restricted cash tied to our China JV for gene therapy manufacturing, our liquidity stands at $2.6 billion—more than sufficient to fund our $1.2 billion committed 2024 R&D spend without dilution.

Total debt remains manageable at $1.1 billion, all non-recourse term loans backed by ZenoVax royalties and milestone streams, yielding a pristine net cash position of $1.7 billion. Our net leverage ratio improved to 0.4x adjusted EBITDA from 0.6x a year ago, reflecting disciplined capital allocation amid rising interest rates. We opportunistically refinanced $300 million of our 2028 notes in July at a blended 4.2% coupon, locking in $50 million in annualized interest savings versus SOFR-plus benchmarks. No near-term maturities until 2026, giving us flexibility as the Fed pivots.

Working capital efficiency continues to shine. Accounts receivable days sales outstanding (DSO) tightened to 52 days from 58 days YoY, driven by faster Medicare Part B reimbursements for ZenoVax in the U.S., where we've captured 22% market share in the RRMM segment per IQVIA data. Inventory levels are optimized at $450 million, up modestly 5% QoQ to support scale-up of our viral vector production for next-gen AAV therapies, but with no excess tied to legacy assets. Payables stretched to 78 days, bolstering our cash conversion cycle to a best-in-class negative 15 days—ahead of peers like Gilead or BeiGene.

Intangibles and goodwill totaled $4.2 billion, bolstered by the $1.1 billion fair value step-up from our acquisition of SynthoRx last year, whose HDAC inhibitor platform is now integral to our combo regimens with PD-1s. We've capitalized $250 million in R&D costs under IFRS 16 for our AI-accelerated small-molecule discovery engine, partnering with Insilico Medicine—yielding three IND-ready candidates already. No impairments this quarter, unlike some sector peers grappling with CRISPR patent cliffs.

Regionally, our U.S. balance sheet strength—75% of cash held stateside—offsets softer Europe collections amid EMA pricing negotiations for ZenoVax, where net prices are holding at €320K per treatment post-HTA reviews in Germany and France. In China, our WuXi AppTec JV contributed $150 million in unrestricted cash from Phase 3 enrollment milestones for our bispecific antibody in NSCLC, with ex-China royalties flowing at 12% on peak sales exceeding RMB 5 billion.

Now, shifting to cash flows, which tell the real story of our transition from biotech burner to cash flow machine. Operating cash flow hit a record $650 million for the quarter, up 32% YoY and 15% sequentially, smashing our $2.0 billion full-year guidance midpoint. This was fueled by ZenoVax gross margins expanding to 92%, with ex-U.S. launches adding $120 million in collections from Japan and Australia. Adjusted for one-time IRA rebate true-ups under the Inflation Reduction Act—net favorable $40 million—our core OCF remains robust at $610 million.

Free cash flow, after $120 million in capex, clocked in at $530 million, representing a 45% FCF margin on adjusted revenues of $1.2 billion. Capex was weighted toward our Singapore biologics facility, now at 70% capacity utilization for mRNA lipid nanoparticle production—a strategic bet mirroring Moderna's playbook to derisk supply chains post-COVID. We're guiding $450-500 million full-year capex, with 60% allocated to tech transfers for our CRISPR/Cas13 hemophilia gene therapy, expecting BLA filing in H2 2025.

Investing activities used $280 million, primarily $200 million upfronts for two Phase 2 oncology deals: one with Merck KGaA on our ADCs, and another licensing claudin-18.2 targets from a Korean biotech. These are high-ROI bets—our internal NPV models project 3x returns on invested capital, akin to the 4.5x uplift from our prior BeiGene ADC pact.

Financing was light at $50 million outflow, comprising $100 million in share repurchases under our $500 million authorization—targeting 2-3% of float annually—and offset by $40 million in employee ESPP proceeds. No new equity; our ATM remains holstered with shares trading at 4.2x 2025E sales, a premium to the XBI index multiple of 3.8x.

YoY trends are telling: OCF conversion hit 115% of net income, up from 95% last year, as we lap R&D normalization post our 2022 PIPE raise. Quarter-over-quarter, FCF grew 22%, outpacing revenue growth thanks to opex leverage—SG&A as a percent of sales dipped to 18% from 22%, driven by commercial team efficiencies and AI tools slashing trial recruitment costs by 30% via our PredictAI platform.

Strategically, these metrics enable three pillars: First, pipeline acceleration—we've ringfenced $800 million for 2025 Phase 3 readouts in ALS and solid tumors, including our IL-12 cytokine now in combo with Keytruda analogs. Second, M&A tuck-ins—with $1.7 billion net cash, we're hunting $200-500 million bolt-ons in radiopharma, scouting assets like Telix's PSMA-617 platform amid the Novartis buyout frenzy. Third, shareholder returns—post-OncoTarget-7 approval, expect FCF payout ratios climbing to 40%, blending dividends and buybacks, while maintaining 18-24 months of cash post-deal.

Looking ahead, we guide FY24 OCF to $2.3-2.5 billion, FCF $1.8-2.0 billion, with balance sheet liquidity >$3 billion by year-end incorporating $500 million in anticipated milestones from Roche and Samsung Bioepis. These positions InnoPharm not just to weather biosimilar headwinds—like the looming Humira erosion—but to capture the $150 billion addressable market in next-gen immuno-oncology by 2030, per Evaluate Pharma forecasts.

Thank you, Johnathan, for that detailed financial overview. As we wrap up our Q3 2024 earnings call for InnoPharm Biotech, I'd like to shift focus to our strategic priorities and the exciting outlook ahead. We've made tremendous strides this quarter, highlighted by the successful U.S. launch of our flagship PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific antibody, NovaLume, which generated $185 million in net sales—exceeding our initial guidance by 15% and capturing 12% market share in the frontline non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) segment within just three months. This momentum underscores our disciplined execution across our three-pillar strategy: Pipeline Acceleration, Global Commercial Expansion, and Innovation Ecosystem Buildout.

Let me start with Pipeline Acceleration, our top priority. We're laser-focused on delivering high-value assets from our oncology and rare disease franchises, where we see the highest unmet needs and blockbuster potential. In oncology, NovaLume's trajectory is phenomenal—our Phase III APEX-301 trial data, presented at ASCO last month, showed a 28% improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) versus Keytruda monotherapy, with a hazard ratio of 0.72. We're on track for a supplemental BLA submission to the FDA by Q4 2024, targeting expansion into triple-negative breast cancer, a $4.5 billion TAM. Complementing this, our next-gen ADC, NovaTox-47—conjugated to our proprietary topoisomerase-1 inhibitor payload—hit 65% objective response rate (ORR) in the ongoing Phase IIb NOVEL-2 study for HER2-low metastatic breast cancer. Enrollment is complete, with topline data expected in Q1 2025, positioning it as a potential rival to Enhertu in a market projected to grow at 22% CAGR through 2030, per IQVIA estimates.

In rare diseases, our gene therapy candidate NV-GT101 for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) remains a game-changer. Following positive 12-month durability data from the Phase I/II LIFT trial—showing 45% microdystrophin expression sustained in treated patients—we've advanced to Phase III initiation this quarter. With a PDUFA target of mid-2026 and Orphan Drug Designation, we anticipate peak sales exceeding $2 billion annually, akin to Sarepta's Elevidys trajectory. R&D investment here is ramping to $450 million for FY2024, up 18% YoY, reflecting our commitment to capitalizing on the $50 billion gene therapy market, which McKinsey forecasts to expand at 35% CAGR.

Turning to Global Commercial Expansion, we're diversifying beyond our U.S.-centric base to mitigate pricing headwinds and tap high-growth regions. In the U.S., NovaLume uptake is stellar, with 75,000 patient starts YTD and gross-to-net adjustments stabilizing at 28%—better than the industry average of 35% amid IRA negotiations. We're guiding for full-year NovaLume sales of $650-700 million, a 5x ramp from launch.

Europe is a bright spot despite NRDL-like reimbursement pressures. Our EMA approval for NovaLume came in May, with launches in Germany, France, and the UK driving €120 million in Q3 sales. We've secured pricing at 92% of list in Germany via our value-based agreement with AOK, mirroring Novartis' strategy with Kisqali. Looking ahead, we expect EMEA revenues to grow 40% to €800 million in FY2025, fueled by 15 ex-U.S. label expansions.

Asia-Pacific is our growth engine. Japan NHI reimbursement for NovaLume at JPY 1.2 million per dose positions us competitively against Opdivo, with Q3 launch on track. In China, our partnership with Sinopharm has accelerated NV-GT101's IND filing— we're targeting CDE approval by 2026, tapping a $10 billion DMD market underserved by global players. Overall, international sales now represent 32% of total revenue, up from 22% last year, and we aim for 45% by 2027 through 20+ partnerships modeled after our Roche collaboration on bispecifics.

Our third pillar, Innovation Ecosystem Buildout, is about future-proofing through tech and M&A. We've invested $120 million in AI-driven drug discovery via our NovaAI platform, partnering with Insilico Medicine. This has de-risked three novel targets in immunology—our IL-23/IL-17 dual inhibitor for psoriasis showed 85% PASI-90 in preclinicals, slashing discovery timelines by 40% versus traditional methods. We're also advancing our CAR-T platform with CRISPR Therapeutics, with NV-CARTx19 entering Phase I for BCMA-refractory multiple myeloma next quarter.

On the M&A front, we closed the $1.8 billion acquisition of Helix BioOncology in June, adding two Phase II assets in PROTACs for solid tumors. This bolsters our $15 billion cash runway through 2028, even at current $1.2 billion annual burn. ESG remains integral—our net-zero R&D facilities and 30% diverse clinical trial enrollment align with stakeholder demands, enhancing our MSCI ESG rating to AA.

Looking to the Outlook: We're raising full-year 2024 guidance to $2.85-2.95 billion in total revenue, implying 25% growth at the midpoint, driven by NovaLume ramp and $300 million from our legacy biosimilars like NovaFilo (pegfilgrastim). Non-GAAP EPS guidance is $1.85-2.05, with adjusted gross margins expanding to 82% on manufacturing efficiencies from our Singapore facility.

For 2025, we project $4.0-4.3 billion revenue, a 42% CAGR trajectory, assuming two approvals (NovaTox-47 and NV-GT101 expansions) and 20% market penetration in new indications. Long-term, our $30 billion peak sales potential by 2030 rests on a 12-asset pipeline, 60% in Phase III or beyond, with oncology comprising 70% of value per NPV modeling.

Risks remain—patent cliffs on legacy products like our infliximab biosimilar erode $200 million annually, offset by 15 new launches through 2027. Macro pressures, including U.S. PBM rebates climbing to 55% and EU HTA harmonization, are navigable via our 360-degree payer strategy. Inflation Reduction Act impacts are minimal, as only 3% of our portfolio hits the $200 million threshold.

In summary, InnoPharm is executing at peak velocity in a biotech landscape ripe for consolidation and innovation. With tailwinds from immunotherapy dominance, gene therapy inflection, and AI efficiencies—echoing peers like Regeneron and Moderna—we're poised for sustained value creation.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call for InnoPharm Biotech. I'm thrilled to dive into one of the standout areas driving our momentum this quarter: our regulatory approvals and label expansions. These milestones not only validate the scientific rigor of our pipeline but also unlock significant commercial upside, positioning us to capture a larger share of high-growth markets in oncology, rare diseases, and cardiometabolics.

Let me start with our flagship achievement: the U.S. FDA approval of our BLA for NVP-301, our next-generation bispecific T-cell engager for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. This approval, which came in ahead of the PDUFA target date on July 15th, builds on the breakthrough therapy designation we secured in Q4 last year. In the pivotal Phase 3 MAGNET-3 trial, NVP-301 demonstrated a 68% overall response rate (ORR) in heavily pretreated patients—median of five prior lines of therapy—including 42% complete responses (CRs), with a median duration of response exceeding 18 months. This outperforms comparators like Janssen's Carvykti, which posted a 98% ORR but in less refractory patients, and positions NVP-301 as a best-in-class option with a cleaner safety profile: cytokine release syndrome (CRS) occurred in only 22% of patients, all Grade 1/2, and neurotoxicity in under 5%.

Commercially, we're projecting peak U.S. sales of $2.8 billion by 2028, up from our prior $2.2 billion estimate, driven by a label that includes patients with high-risk cytogenetics like del(17p). Launch is underway with our expanded U.S. specialty pharmacy network, and we've already secured J-code reimbursement from CMS, with initial uptake mirroring the rapid 25% market share gain seen with Regeneron's Linvoseltamab earlier this year. Internationally, the EMA's CHMP issued a positive opinion last week, paving the way for full approval by Q4, while our Japanese PMDA filing is on track for a 2025 readout—Japan's myeloma market, valued at $1.2 billion, remains underserved post-Kyprolis patent expiry.

Moving to label expansions, we achieved two major sNDA approvals that materially broaden our existing blockbusters. First, BPI-456, our PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), received FDA expansion into frontline maintenance therapy following chemo-immunotherapy. The supporting data from the Phase 3 LUNG-X trial showed a 28% reduction in progression-free survival (PFS) risk—median PFS of 14.2 months versus 10.8 for placebo—mirroring the hazard ratio benefits of AstraZeneca's Imfinzi but with 15% lower immune-related adverse events (irAEs). This expansion adds an estimated 150,000 eligible U.S. patients annually, boosting our 2024 revenue guidance for BPI-456 by $350 million to $1.75 billion total, with ex-U.S. sales accelerating via our partnership with Roche in Europe and Asia-Pacific. In China, the NMPA granted conditional approval for this indication just yesterday, tapping into a $3 billion NSCLC market growing at 12% CAGR amid rising smoking prevalence.

Second, our GLP-1 receptor agonist Metavex earned FDA label expansion for chronic kidney disease (CKD) in Type 2 diabetes patients, based on the landmark Phase 3 FLOW trial subset analysis. Here, Metavex reduced the composite kidney endpoint by 24% (HR 0.76), with eGFR slope preservation outperforming Lilly's Mounjaro in head-to-head modeling. This is huge: CKD affects 40 million U.S. adults, and with Medicare Part D redesign favoring high-value cards like ours, we're forecasting an incremental $1.2 billion in U.S. peak sales by 2027. Europe followed suit with EMA approval last month, and we're in late-stage talks with India's CDSCO—where diabetes prevalence hits 11%—for a low-cost biosimilar pathway to accelerate access.

Regionally, these wins reflect our global strategy: 60% of our approvals this year are U.S.-led, but EU and Asia contribute 25% and 15% respectively, diversifying revenue amid U.S. pricing pressures from the Inflation Reduction Act. Trends-wise, we've benefited from FDA's accelerated pathways—three of our five 2024 submissions leveraged RMAT or Fast Track—reducing timelines by 18 months on average versus traditional NDAs. Safety remains our north star: across programs, our adverse event discontinuation rates average 4%, well below the 8-10% industry benchmark from recent IQVIA data.

Strategically, these approvals de-risk our pipeline and fuel M&A optionality. We've accelerated two readouts into 2025: a NVP-301 combo with our ADCs in myeloma, and BPI-456 frontline data. In the Pharma and Biotech sectors, the patent cliff remains a perennial challenge, much like the seismic revenue erosions we saw with Pfizer's Lipitor in 2011, where U.S. sales plummeted over 80% within two years post-generic entry, or Merck's Singulair, which lost $4.5 billion in peak sales by 2013. Oncology leader BioVaxfen (BTK inhibitor, in the ibrutinib class like AbbVie's Imbruvica) contributes another $850 million, with core patents lapsing in 2027. Regionally tailored tactics amplify this. In China, our JX partnership for localized manufacturing has secured NRDL inclusion, mitigating 40% erosion risks seen in peers like Regeneron's Dupixent analogs.

R&D intensity remains at 22% of sales, fueling $2.5 billion in annual LCM investments, complemented by bolt-on M&A like our $1.2 billion acquisition of LCM Therapeutics last year for their PROTAC platform. Risks remain—Paragraph IV litigations are ongoing with five challengers for NovaLizumab, and biosimilar pricing could undercut 30-40%—but our track record speaks volumes: post-cliff, we've historically retained 25-30% of revenues through Year 3 via LCM, outperforming industry averages of 15-20%.
